Given that the differential equation 

$$
7\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+14y=21{e}^{-5x}
$$

has the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{-2x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

We see that the right-hand side is $21{e}^{-5x},$ and ${e}^{-5x}$ is not a term in the complementary solution, so we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha {e}^{-5x},
$$

where $\alpha $ is a constant that is to be determined.

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-5\alpha {e}^{-5x}
$$

To find the value of $\alpha ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}7(-5\alpha {e}^{-5x})+14(\alpha {e}^{-5x}) & =21{e}^{-5x} \\ (-35+14)\alpha {e}^{-5x} & =21{e}^{-5x} \\ -21\alpha {e}^{-5x} & =21{e}^{-5x} \\ \alpha  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-{e}^{-5x}.
$$
